name: Clear Roads — Baseline
description: No hazards. All roads are open. Use this scenario to compare the three algorithms on an unobstructed network. Notice how BFS minimises hops (not distance), while A* finds the lowest-cost route by combining real distance with a heuristic.
teaching_note: Expected: BFS finds a 6-hop path. Greedy may find a longer path by always heading toward the destination. A* finds the minimum-cost path.

name: Domlur Underpass Flooded
description: The Airport Road underpass at Domlur (N5-N8 direct link) is blocked by floodwater. Algorithms must find an alternative route through Domlur Junction (N6). This demonstrates how all three algorithms dynamically reroute around a single blocked road.
teaching_note: With N5-N8 blocked, algorithms must go through N6 (Domlur). Watch how BFS finds a longer hop path while A* finds the lowest-cost detour.

name: Eastern Flood Spreading
description: Heavy flooding in the eastern corridor: the Domlur to Indiranagar road (N6-N7) is fully blocked by a canal overflow, and two roads approaching Domlur (N3-N5 and N5-N6) are risky due to waterlogging. Algorithms must weigh the penalty of risky roads versus longer but safer detours.
teaching_note: BFS ignores risk penalties and finds a hop-optimal path. A* accounts for the +500m penalty on risky roads and may prefer a longer but cheaper (risk-adjusted) route. Compare their total_cost vs total_distance_m values.
